meta.title: Who funds El Niño coordination
meta.status: First draft. Figures come from public pages read on the as-of date. Anything marked VERIFY was not checked against a primary document or is the author's reading. 'Fit' and the links to problems are judgement, meant to be argued with.

convene.name: Convening and joint planning
convene.desc: Dialogue platforms, working groups, shared calendars, bringing mandates into one room.

data.name: Shared data and interoperability
data.desc: Common data standards, open platforms, information management that many actors use.

finance.name: Aligning finance
finance.desc: Making pooled funds, insurance and loans fit together, pre-agreeing who pays for what.

voice.name: Local voice and legitimacy
voice.desc: Locally led decisions, participation and deliberation over triggers and targeting.

learning.name: Learning and accountability
learning.desc: Evidence, shared definitions of success, after-action reviews, keeping lessons between events.

tools.name: Open tools
tools.desc: Free and open-source software and data that coordination runs on.

funders.name: German Federal Foreign Office
funders.what: The largest donor to anticipatory action. Funds the Anticipation Hub, its dialogue platforms and the annual global overview of anticipatory action, as well as Red Cross, Start Network and UN anticipatory programmes.
funders.money: In the Hub's 2025 overview, Germany is reported as the source of 58% of recorded 2024 funding for building and financing frameworks. VERIFY against the report's donor section.
funders.access: No open calls. Money flows through German Red Cross, UN agencies and German NGOs; coordination work gets funded as part of their programmes.
src: Anticipatory Action in 2025: A Global Overview (Anticipation Hub, 28 May 2026)

funders.name: Anticipation Hub
funders.kind: Coordination platform (German Red Cross, IFRC, Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre)
funders.what: Knowledge and exchange platform founded in 2020 with more than 170 partners. Runs working groups and regional dialogue platforms, publishes the yearly global overview, and co-chairs with REAP a community on linking risk finance and anticipatory action.
funders.money: Funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. Does not run open grant calls.
funders.access: Join a working group or dialogue platform; propose shared products (such as this map) as a joint output.
src: FCDO joins as a partner (29 June 2021)

funders.name: CREWS (Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems)
funders.kind: Multi-donor trust fund (12 contributing countries; implemented by WMO, World Bank/GFDRR, UNDRR, ITU, IFRC)
funders.what: Funds early-warning systems in Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States, including the dissemination and coordination parts of Early Warnings for All. In February 2026 it approved funding for REAP's convenings, knowledge products, 'networks of networks' labs and information management.
funders.money: USD 1,942,957 approved for REAP for 2026–27 (22nd Steering Committee, 13 February 2026), with a view to three more years if funds allow.
funders.access: Through its implementing partners and REAP. Country projects are proposed by governments with WMO, World Bank or UNDRR.

funders.name: REAP (Risk-informed Early Action Partnership)
funders.kind: Partnership network, secretariat hosted by IFRC
funders.what: The broadest network of early-warning and early-action actors, with more than 100 partners. Not a grant-maker, but it holds coordination money: convenings, policy retreats, a policy academy and regional secondees.
funders.money: Funded largely by CREWS (see above). The CREWS paper puts REAP at about 0.33% of a roughly USD 480 million annual early-warning and early-action budget.
funders.access: Become a partner; offer facilitation or shared tools to its labs and convenings.

funders.name: Start Network
funders.kind: Network of NGOs with pooled funds
funders.what: Members decide collectively how pooled money is used. Start Fund pays out fast on member alerts; Start Ready pre-arranges money and plans for Somalia, Zimbabwe, Madagascar, Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan, the Philippines and Guatemala. Analysis for Action and Anticipatory Action Plan grants pay for joint risk analysis and planning.
funders.money: El Niño amounts not published in the May 2026 member blog. VERIFY.
funders.access: Members only. Outsiders can work as analysts or facilitators for a member.

funders.name: OCHA: anticipatory action frameworks, Centre for Humanitarian Data
funders.what: OCHA builds the country frameworks that tie a trigger to pre-agreed money and plans across agencies, and its Centre for Humanitarian Data runs HDX, the shared humanitarian data platform.
funders.money: Coordination is paid from OCHA's own budget; the Centre for Humanitarian Data's funding was not checked. VERIFY.
funders.access: Data partnerships and contributions to HDX; work with country offices on frameworks.

funders.name: Global Shield against Climate Risks
funders.what: Helps climate-vulnerable countries put pre-arranged financial protection in place through an in-country process that brings ministries, donors and insurers together. Three financing vehicles: the Global Shield Solutions Platform, the Global Shield Financing Facility and the V20 Joint Multi-Donor Fund.
funders.money: Amounts not checked. VERIFY. The Secretariat moved to the Frankfurt School of Finance & Management on 1 January 2026.
funders.access: Through the vehicles' implementing partners in each country (Pakistan and Malawi have started).
src: Global Shield Secretariat joins Frankfurt School (19 Dec 2025)

funders.name: UK FCDO and the Centre for Disaster Protection
funders.kind: Government donor and the advisory centre it funds
funders.what: FCDO became the Anticipation Hub's second donor-government partner in 2021 and funds research such as SHEAR, the largest research project on anticipatory action. The Centre for Disaster Protection advises governments on pre-arranged finance.
funders.money: Current amounts not checked. VERIFY.
funders.access: Research consortia and the Centre's advisory work; no open grants found.

funders.name: World Bank GFDRR
funders.kind: Multi-donor trust fund for disaster risk
funders.what: Technical assistance to governments on risk finance and risk data, including open risk data work. Also an implementing partner of CREWS.
funders.money: Current funding windows not checked. VERIFY.
funders.access: Through World Bank country teams and consultancy contracts.

funders.name: CAF, Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean
funders.what: Financing, technical assistance, humanitarian aid and information-exchange mechanisms for floods, drought and forest fires. Preparing a white paper with recommendations.
funders.money: USD 1 billion for 2026–27 (announced 2 October 2026). CAF Forum in Panama, 27–28 January 2027.
funders.access: Governments borrow. The white paper and the January forum are openings to bring shared coordination products to the table.

funders.name: Climate Justice Resilience Fund
funders.what: Grants to women-, youth- and Indigenous-led groups for community-led climate resilience, including loss and damage grants in East Africa, Bangladesh and India and a small-grants pilot.
funders.money: Generally up to USD 250,000, through open calls and letters of inquiry. Current status unclear. VERIFY at cjrfund.org.
funders.access: Local organisations apply directly.

funders.name: NLnet
funders.what: Grants for free and open-source software and open data, open to individuals as well as organisations. A fit for open coordination and deliberation tools of the kind listed on the problem map.
funders.money: EUR 5,000–50,000 for a first grant. Deadlines on the 3rd of every odd month; next one 3 January 2027, 12:00 CET. EU-funded calls need a European dimension; proposals must be written by humans.
funders.access: Apply directly.

funders.name: FLOSS/fund
funders.what: Sustains existing, widely used open-source projects; individuals can apply. Relevant once a shared coordination tool has real users.
funders.money: From USD 10,000 in steps of USD 25,000, up to USD 100,000 a year. Reviewed every quarter. Very new projects are not considered.
funders.access: Publish a funding.json manifest in the repository and submit its URL.

funders.name: Elrha (HIF and R2HC)
funders.what: Funds humanitarian innovation and health research. As of November 2026 the only open call is an expression of interest for an anchor institution in a climate-and-health collaborative in Ethiopia, for established organisations.
funders.money: No open general call.
funders.access: Watch the funding page; research partners apply.

funders.name: Large philanthropy: Rockefeller Foundation, Wellcome, Z Zurich Foundation, Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
funders.what: Fund climate and health (heat, disease), community flood resilience and data for public good. They rarely fund coordination on its own, but sometimes fund the platform a field shares.
funders.money: Multi-year programmes, usually by invitation. Not checked for 2026–27. VERIFY.
funders.access: Through organisations they already fund.

funders.name: CERF anticipatory action window
funders.what: Releases pre-agreed money to UN agencies when a framework's trigger is reached.
funders.money: Up to USD 100 million for El Niño (announced 13 July 2026); more than USD 20 million already allocated to six countries. In March 2026, CERF-funded activations in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras mobilised USD 10.5 million for up to 145,000 people.
funders.access: UN agencies only.

funders.name: FAO and WFP joint anticipatory action appeal
funders.what: Anticipatory action for food and livelihoods, June 2026 to March 2027.
funders.money: USD 202 million for about 8.8 million people in 22 countries. How much is funded was not checked. VERIFY.
funders.access: Donors give; FAO and WFP implement.

funders.name: IFRC DREF and Early Action Protocols
funders.what: National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies draw on DREF's anticipatory pillar through pre-approved Early Action Protocols, and on DREF for response.
funders.money: El Niño 2026 amounts not found. VERIFY.
funders.access: National Societies only.
src: IFRC: preparing for El Niño in Latin America and the Caribbean

funders.name: World Bank crisis instruments (CERC, Rapid Response Option, Cat DDO, IDA Crisis Response Window)
funders.what: Contingent and emergency lending to governments.
funders.money: Kenya: about USD 400 million expected through the Rapid Response Option (Reuters, 10 September 2026; disbursement not confirmed). Marshall Islands: USD 11 million for El Niño and dengue.
funders.access: Governments only.

funders.name: Sovereign risk pools: ARC, CCRIF SPC, PCRIC, SEADRIF
funders.what: Pay governments when a drought, cyclone or rainfall index is triggered. After the 2023–24 El Niño, ARC paid out about USD 60 million in southern Africa.
funders.money: 2026–27 payouts not yet found. VERIFY.
funders.access: Member governments.
